options: Any production server that happens to get scanned occasionally
A firewall configured with extra logging enabled
A decoy system or service with no legitimate business purpose, deployed to attract and detect unauthorized activity
A backup server that real users log into once a month
questions.explain: A honeypot's defining trait is that it serves no legitimate business purpose at all — nothing real should ever need to touch it.

questions.q: Why is any interaction with a honeypot inherently suspicious?
options: Because no real user or process should ever have a reason to touch it, so there's no legitimate baseline to confuse the signal
Because honeypots are always placed outside the firewall
Because honeypots automatically block all traffic by default
Because only administrators are physically able to reach a honeypot
questions.explain: A honeypot's normal state is silence — it has no legitimate traffic to sort through, unlike a real production server.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the three real jobs a honeypot does, as described in this lesson?
options: Acting as an early warning system that catches an attacker already inside the network
Replacing the need for a firewall entirely
Automatically patching vulnerable software on the real network
Encrypting all traffic that passes through the internal VLAN
questions.explain: Honeypots provide early warning, let defenders study attacker behavior safely, and can slow attackers down as a tarpit.

questions.q: In the FINANCE-BACKUP-2024 example, why does a single login attempt trigger a high-confidence alert?
options: Because no legitimate application, user, or process is ever configured to connect to that decoy share
Because the login attempt came from an external IP address
Because the share contains real, highly sensitive financial data
Because the share was scheduled for a backup job at that exact time
questions.explain: Since nothing legitimate ever touches the decoy share, the login attempt itself is the evidence of unauthorized activity.

questions.q: What is a honeypot 'tarpit' behavior intended to do?
options: Waste an attacker's time and resources on something that was never real
Encrypt the attacker's connection for later forensic review
Automatically report attackers to law enforcement
Speed up legitimate network traffic during peak hours
questions.explain: A tarpit deliberately slows interaction down or offers fake resources to explore, buying defenders time while the attacker is occupied.
